x.h: A Charge against the People. (b. c. 706.)
p: When our Lord Jesus promised to send the Comforter he added, When he shall come he shall convince (John xvi. 7, 8); for conviction must prepare for comfort, and must also separate between the precious and the vile, and mark out those to whom comfort does not belong.

x.h: A Charge against the People. (b. c. 706.)
p: It concerns us therefore to enquire, on a fast-day, what it is that will be acceptable to God, and afflictive to our corrupt nature, and tending to its mortification.

x.h: A Charge against the People; Encouragement to Israelites Indeed. (b. c. 706.)
p: A further account of the duty to be done in order to our interest in these promises (v. 9, 10); and here, as before, it is required that we both do justly and love mercy, that we cease to do evil and learn to do well. We must abstain from all acts of violence and fraud.

We must abound in all acts of charity and beneficence. We must not only give alms according as the necessities of the poor require, but, We must give freely and cheerfully, and from a principle of charity.

x.h: The Sanctification of the Sabbath. (b. c. 706.)
p: We shall have the comfort of it; the work will be its own wages. If we call the sabbath a delight, then shall we delight ourselves in the Lord; he will more and more manifest himself to us as the delightful subject of our thoughts and meditations and the delightful object of our best affections. Note, The more pleasure we take in serving God the more pleasure we shall find in it.
